quickAnswer: To verify a plastic surgeon in Türkiye, cross-check their name on the official TPRECD doctor directory, search the EBOPRAS Fellows register if they claim European board fellowship, and confirm their operating hospital holds a Turkish Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate with on-site ICU and anesthesiology backup.

body.text: How do you check Turkish Plastic Surgery Board (TPRECD) and EBOPRAS membership?

Verify national plastic surgery credentials on the public [TPRECD Doctor Search directory](https://www.plastikcerrahi.org.tr/doktor-arama), which lists active members of the Turkish Society of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons alongside their affiliated institutions. To check European fellowship, search the surgeon's full name on the official [EBOPRAS Fellows register](https://ebopras.eu/fellows).

Per [TPRECD membership criteria](https://dernek.plastikcerrahi.org.tr/menu/16/uyelik-icin-gerekli-belgeler), full membership requires a verified medical degree, a completed plastic surgery specialty diploma, two full-member references, and adherence to the society's ethics declaration. Under [EBOPRAS examination rules](https://ebopras.eu/examination/ebopras-examination), surgeons earn the FEBOPRAS title only after passing both the computer-based Part 1 MCQ exam and the live Part 2 oral exam. Note that EBOPRAS explicitly advises confirming active good standing through national medical authorities.

body.text: Why does the hospital's ICU and emergency backup matter as much as the surgeon?

Even a highly trained surgeon cannot compensate for an under-equipped operating facility if rare anesthesia reactions, airway issues, or post-operative bleeding occur. Operating inside a full-service, accredited hospital provides immediate access to an on-site intensive care unit (ICU), blood bank, diagnostic imaging, and 24-hour multi-specialty physicians.

The [ISAPS Safety Diamond](https://www.isaps.org/media/dydp5pmm/montserrat_medical-tourism-english.pdf) places facility accreditation alongside surgeon certification as a core pillar of patient safety abroad. Always verify that the specific hospital—not merely a marketing agency or consultation office—appears on the Turkish Ministry of Health's [list of authorized health tourism hospitals](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) and holds formal hospital privileges for your named surgeon.
How do you confirm the named surgeon performs the entire operation?

Confirm your named surgeon performs every critical step by requesting their full legal name on both the written surgical consent form and the operating-room schedule before paying a deposit. Ask directly during video and in-person consultations which portions—if any—are assisted by residents, junior doctors, or nurses.

body.text: What pre-op bloodwork and anesthesiologist clearance are mandatory?

Before general anesthesia in Türkiye, standard hospital protocols require an in-person pre-operative assessment with a licensed anesthesiologist, complete blood count (CBC), coagulation panel (PT/INR, aPTT), basic metabolic and liver-kidney panels, viral screening, and an electrocardiogram (ECG) or chest imaging based on age and medical history.

According to [NHS pre-operative assessment guidance](https://www.esht.nhs.uk/service/anaesthetics/pre-operative-assessment/) and [NHS general anaesthesia standards](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/general-anaesthesia/), pre-surgery screening identifies hidden anemia, clotting risks, medication interactions, or uncontrolled blood pressure before you enter theater. Never skip fasting rules or conceal nicotine, herbal supplements, or prescription medicines; honest disclosure allows your anesthesiologist to postpone or adjust care safely if abnormal lab values appear.

faq.q: Is every doctor who performs cosmetic surgery in Türkiye a plastic surgeon?
faq.a: No. ENT specialists often perform rhinoplasty, oculoplastic ophthalmologists perform eyelid surgery, and dermatologists perform non-surgical aesthetics. Always verify that your doctor's formal specialty diploma matches the exact procedure you plan to undergo.

faq.q: Does a clinic's Ministry of Health Health Tourism Certificate guarantee surgical quality?
faq.a: No. The certificate confirms legal authorization, foreign-language staffing, and regulatory compliance to treat international patients, but it does not replace verifying the individual surgeon's board credentials, portfolio, and hospital ICU capabilities.

faq.q: What if a surgeon is not listed on the EBOPRAS directory?
faq.a: EBOPRAS is a voluntary European board examination, not a legal prerequisite to practice in Türkiye. Many respected Turkish plastic surgeons hold national TPRECD certification without sitting EBOPRAS, though FEBOPRAS status provides an additional verified benchmark.

faq.q: Can I do my pre-op bloodwork at home before flying to Istanbul?
faq.a: Home bloodwork can help flag major issues like severe anemia early, but Turkish hospitals almost always repeat mandatory lab panels and an in-person anesthesiologist exam locally before clearing you for theater.

faq.q: What should I do if a clinic refuses to name my surgeon before I book?
faq.a: Walk away. Legitimate surgical practices identify your operating physician clearly during pre-consultation so you can verify their specialty registration, hospital privileges, and unedited case history before committing.
